analysis:
The change is documentation only, in docs/developer/threat-model-review.md. It describes CI review tooling (threat-review workflow, Bedrock/OpenRouter routing, merge-clearance policy) and does not touch the provider runtime, coordinator contract, keys, attestation, the prefix cache or any other asset in the canonical threat model. No canonical threat IDs (A-*, TB-*, T-*) are directly affected.

Changes examined:
- Head lines 10-11, 79-82 and 125: manual paid depth requests are removed. Only the unpaid preflight dispatch remains, and job reruns do not start paid work. This narrows spend and attack surface rather than widening it.
- Head lines 140-159 and 174-176: the fixed call limit becomes a workload-based allowance with a 100-call emergency ceiling, a shared repair slot, and a 3000s scan timeout inside a 60-minute job. This is a documented cost/availability policy. The doc states that oversized stages are refused and require human review. I cannot verify that budget_scan.py and the workflow implement it, because those files are outside the supplied evidence.
- Head lines 224-225: after a member is removed, the guidance changes from rerunning the security workflow to requiring independent human review. This is a conservative change.
- Head lines 315-317 and 330-340: failed scans are handed to a human reviewer instead of a paid rerun. A timeout (SCAN_TIMEOUT) requires human review.
- Head lines 422-424: the doc states that human-review handoffs do not activate conditional clearance or author auto-merge.

No security regression or invalidated threat-model assumption was identified in the supplied text. The remaining integration question is whether the accompanying workflow and script changes match this documentation. That includes removal of the workflow_dispatch PR input, a permission check, and the BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY, BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS and THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS settings. Those files are not in this batch, so the documented controls are unverified here.
